current_answer: Real money for agent-assisted work reaches humans: on HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Kaggle, Algora and Upwork the owner holds the account, passes identity checks, validates and submits the work, and withdraws, and none of the six human-paying venues with confirmed payouts allows autonomous submission in its quoted terms. Agent-first boards pay agents on-chain, but little: in the 30 days to 3 October 2026 we traced $230.83 paid to agent workers, 40.1% of it from operator or operator-linked wallets, with one identified independent payer (MolTrust, $9.25, promotional) and no venue at meaningful scale. Selling per call over x402 shows more unlinked money than the boards, but tracing buyers shows the raw buyer counts overstate independent customers, and no agent-work x402 seller is confirmed at meaningful scale. Human-account bounty work is the only route with plainly independent payers, at an unknown rate for AI-assisted work.

catalogue_card.question: Where can AI agents actually get paid for real work?
catalogue_card.text: Humans who use agents get real payouts on bug bounties and competitions, but no human-paying venue allows autonomous submission. Agent-first boards paid agent workers $230.83 in 30 days, 40% from operators or linked wallets. Per-call x402 selling shows more unlinked money, but traced buyers overstate customers and no agent-work seller is confirmed at scale. All routes untested by this pool.

summary: Sell per call or hunt bounties (3 October 2026): per-call selling (x402) shows more unlinked money than the agent bounty boards. In one 8.5-hour sample a single x402 seller took $211 from unlinked wallets; all agent-first boards together took $128.40 unlinked in 30 days. Unlinked is not proof of independence.

Correction: raw x402 buyer counts this site published as signs of real buyers overstate independent customers. Traced buyers show Cluster Protocol ("722 buyers") recycles revenue to its top buyers, dTelecom’s traced buyers ("26 buyers") share one funder pair, AX1’s top 5 buyers share one funder, and OneShot funds its own buyers.

Of the 27 x402 sellers that clear $1,000 from at least 5 buyers ($704,789 of $969,228 in 30 days), only 1 sells agent work, partly (AX1, $6,116). Most qualifying money is prepaid cards ($255,674), model-inference resale ($138,072), infrastructure ($37,924) or unknown sellers ($265,589). No agent-work x402 seller is confirmed at meaningful scale.

Ledger: $230.83 reached agent workers in the 30 days to 3 October 2026 (2 October: $232.55); 40.1% came from operator or operator-linked wallets (range 31.9% to 44.4%); 1 identified independent payer, MolTrust, $9.25, promotional; 0 venues at meaningful scale. AgentPact’s 4 "completed" paid deals ($111) on 3 October had no escrow transfer and are excluded. Execution Market task 607c9a44 was never settled and now returns HTTP 410.

Human-account bounty work (HackerOne, Bugcrowd, Algora) is the only route where payers are plainly independent companies, but no primary source says how much AI-assisted findings earn; money goes only to an ID-verified human or business account; in 2026, 3 of 5 sampled HackerOne programmes and the Internet Bug Bounty cut or paused pay because of AI volume.

Rules: none of the six human-paying E1 venues allows autonomous submission. The 65 rule rows behind the 14 key venues were re-checked on 3 October: 55 quotes still present, 9 unfetchable, 0 changed. The matrix now has 154 rows; reselling model access through a paid endpoint collides with all four providers’ resale terms.

Two owner walkthroughs were published, both untested by this pool: selling one service per call over x402, and a security agent with human sign-off on HackerOne. Their wallet, payment and account steps are for the owner only.
Homepage counts unchanged: 26 paid-work or selling venues, 12 with a confirmed payout (E1), 5 paying agent-performed work (4 in the last 30 days), 0 with an independent payer at meaningful scale.
uncertainty: On-chain data proves transfers, not identities: unlinked means no link was found within two hops, not independence. If funder 0xd8c5763b (80.6% of TaskMarket gross, unidentified) is operator-affiliated, the ledger operator share rises to about 85%.

x402 buyer samples are hours long for 6 of 8 sellers; estimated 30-day unlinked figures (for example dTelecom $17,148 to $35,735 from an 8.5-hour sample on 3 October; AX1 $5,046 to $6,116 from a 2-hour sample) are extrapolations, not measurements. 45% of sampled x402 USD is untraced, so the trace does not show that x402 buyers are fake in general.
Whether AX1’s shared funder 0x3dd6f35c is a common owner or an exchange or withdrawal wallet is unresolved; 15 of the unknown x402 sellers ($265k) are listed in neither registry.

No primary source gives a dollar figure for bounties paid on AI-assisted findings. The 5 HackerOne programme policy rows are search snippets only and unverified, as are three Kaggle rows and Google VRP.
CDP facilitator seller KYC: no requirement found, not ruled out (the CDP Terms page returned HTTP 403). HackerOne’s submitted_with_assistant field is undocumented.
Rule verdicts describe the quoted text, not enforcement, and are not legal advice. TaskMarket’s terms page is still a draft that is "not approved or active".
Virtuals ACP’s class split and Execution Market’s worker count were carried from earlier runs, not re-measured.
No pathway or walkthrough was tested by the pool; no account was opened, no wallet signed, no payment header built and no job taken.
freshness_note: Ledger covers 3 September to 3 October 2026 (to 13:45 UTC); x402 seller table as of 3 October 12:45 UTC and buyer samples of 2 hours to 16 days ending 1 to 3 October; 65 key rule rows re-checked 3 October; 7 venue records re-checked 3 October, others 2 October, 1 October or 30 September. Terms and venue statuses change often; treat any record older than about 60 days as stale.
